newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown drops to 9-mo low vs mark/dollar peg. [CORRECTED 18:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech crown drops to 9-mo low vs mark/dollar peg. [CORRECTED 18:39 GMT]

text.p: The Czech crown on Thursday fell to a 9-month low against its mark/dollar basket, as nervous foreign investors sold the currency ahead of Friday's 1996 GDP and Monday's February trade data.
(Corrects headline and first para' from "12-month low").

By mid-afternoon the crown was trading at 29.251 to the dollar and 17.458 to the mark, or 0.95 percent above parity with the basket, well below Wednesday's central bank fixing at 29.072 and 17.277 or 1.81 percent.
Dealers said the crown found its floor in heavy activity midday at +0.8 percent above parity and then recovered a bit.
"We are looking at Friday's GDP data and Monday's trade figures... Foreigners have been selling crowns, I think that's a good strategy," said dealer Jakub Perina at Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

A Reuters survey of economists on Thursday showed fourth quarter GDP was expected to ease to about 3.4 percent, year-on-year, with full-year growth at 3.6 percent, short of revised government forecasts of more than four percent growth for the year.
A slowdown in industrial output in the early part of the year also has analysts expecting an already poor trade deficit to get worse.
Perina said he thought the crown might test +0.5 percent percent above parity.
"If the index will break (+0.5 percent), we will go to parity," he said.
